title: Lyceum Health - Dossier + Cold Sequence
content:
SUMMARY:
Quick internal sketch for outbound into Lyceum Health (regional telehealth chain, ~120 clinics across three states). Objective: pitch a 6-week inference pilot to replace their on-prem LLM proxy for automated triage and discharge summaries — emphasis on predictable latency and data isolation (PHI).

RESEARCH NOTES (quick hits):
- HQ: Portland, OR; primary EMR: MediSuite (custom integration).
- Recent signal: Series B announced Nov 2024; hiring for ML infra role (LinkedIn) — likely momentum and budget window.
- CTO is Priya Malhotra (background: Pager/athena), head of ML Ops is likely an early advocate.
- Compliance focus: HITRUST & SOC2 discussions in PR/earnings. They repeatedly call out "PHI zoning" in public materials.
- Current gap: they run a narrow LLM locally for triage but suffer big tail latency spikes on clinic hours and operational overhead for updates.
- Value props that resonate: private deployment, guaranteed latency SLOs, deterministic cost per token, and can fall back to smaller quantized models when load spikes.

STAKEHOLDERS (initial list):
- Priya Malhotra — CTO (eval + signoff influence)
- Miguel Alvarez — Head of Clinical Ops (use-case owner)
- Lena Cho — Security/Privacy lead (compliance gating)
- Rajesh Kumar — VP Engineering (budget owner)

TRIGGERS / ANGLES / OPENING HYPOTHESES:
1) Rapid B2B growth after Series B → need to stop over-indexing on ad-hoc infra. Sell predictable unit economics + a path to Dedicated.
2) PHI concerns: emphasize Private (VPC, on-prem optional) + KMS/HSM + audit logs.
3) Triage latency pains: show per-route latency dashboards + token-level cost breakdowns (console).
4) Eval runway: offer a timeboxed 6-week pilot with 2 clinic integrations and SLO targets.

COLD EMAIL SEQUENCE (high-variance, keep short):
Email 1 (intro) — Subject ideas: "Can Redwood help Lyceum hit triage SLAs?"
Hi {{first_name}},
I noticed Lyceum’s recent expansion and your emphasis on secure, reliable triage. We help health systems run LLM inference with predictable latency, PHI controls, and cost visibility — often enabling a 2–4x reduction in operational overhead vs DIY inference.
Could we book 20 min to show a short pilot plan tailored to clinic integration?
— Samir (Redwood Inference)

Email 2 (2–3 days later) — Subject: "Pilot idea: 6 weeks, PHI-safe triage, measurable SLOs"
Quick follow on: proposed pilot = 6 weeks, 2 clinics, private control plane + dedicated capacity during clinic hours, success metric = 95th pct latency < 300ms for triage flows. Happy to share a checklist for integration.

Email 3 (value proof) — Subject: "Example: rural health network cut latency spikes by 70%"
One pager (attach): case study of a regional health partner who moved from a mixed on-prem setup to a dedicated deployment and removed manual cache invalidation work.

LINKED VOICEMAIL / TALK TRACK (for discovery call):
- Quick intro, 60s value summary: predictable latency, PHI controls, visible unit economics.
- Ask: current triage SLA, busiest hours, existing LLM infra pain points.
- If they say integration is hard -> say we provide connectors + SRE assistance for pilot (2-week ramp).

OBJECTION MAP / Q&A (raw):
- "We can just host it ourselves":
  * A: Totally — but many teams underestimate tail-latency engineering. We provide a runtime with smart routing, caching, and SLA-backed Dedicated options so you get predictable behavior without hiring 3x people to babysit.
- "Cost concerns":
  * A: Offer an initial pilot on Redwood Dedicated with fixed monthly committed nodes for the test window. Show example cost model (console token-level breakdown) and simulation of their triage workload.
- "PHI/compliance":
  * A: Private control plane + VPC peering + KMS/HSM key policies + audit logs. Provide SOC2 + HITRUST mapping doc during technical deep dive.
- "Lock-in worries":
  * A: We support model pinning, exportable KV caches, and an option to run a private control plane so your config is portable. Also emphasize fallbacks to compatible open-model variants.

PILOT SCOPE (6 weeks suggested):
- Week 0–1: Kickoff, security questionnaire, network setup (VPC peering), identify 2 pilot clinics.
- Week 2: Baseline collection + latency/cost metrics on their current infra.
- Week 3–4: Deploy Redwood Private (dedicated pool), integrate triage service endpoint, run controlled traffic.
- Week 5: Observe, tweak batching/quantization profiles, enable per-route caching.
- Week 6: Finalize success metrics, handoff runbook, ROI estimate for org-wide rollout.

KPIs TO TRACK DURING PILOT:
- 95th percentile latency for triage flows (target < 300ms)
- Average tokens per request, token cost per triage event
- Number of manual incidents (before vs during pilot)
- Time to model rollouts / version changes (minutes vs days)

MEETING PREP (if call booked):
- Have short console demo showing latency traces + token cost table for a sample prompt.
- Bring SRE checklist + network diagram for VPC peering.
- Security one-pager mapped to HITRUST controls ready to send.

OPEN QUESTIONS (to research before outreach):
- Confirm whether Lyceum stores PHI in prompts or in EMR pointer references (this dictates caching decisions).
- Get rough triage request volume per clinic per day — need to simulate to size Dedicated nodes.
- Does their MediSuite integration support webhooks for async responses? If not, discuss streaming response strategy.

NEXT STEPS / TODOs (me):
- [ ] Draft one-pager case study with anonymized numbers (ask PM Evelyn for metrics).
- [ ] Mock console demo using synthetic triage prompts (Jonah to help setup model profile).
- [ ] Pull Lyceum job posts + recent press to use in email personalization.
- [ ] Draft security mapping doc snippet for HITRUST -> Redwood features and attach to email 2.

RISK NOTES / CONCERNS:
- If Lyceum insists on fully air-gapped on-prem for PHI, pilot scope expands (need on-site deployment team + infra budget).
- Their EMR connector could be the slowest path; plan for a lightweight adapter to pass prompts and receive structured responses.

Rough cold call script (30s):
"Hi {{first_name}}, I’m Samir from Redwood Inference. Quick question — are triage teams at Lyceum seeing unpredictable delays from your LLM tooling during peak hours? We help health systems run private, SLA-backed inference that reduces tail latency and gives visibility into per-request cost. Can we book 20 minutes to walk through a short pilot?"

NOTES TO SELF: keep messages concrete — cite numbers (95th pct latency, pilot duration) instead of vague benefits. Avoid heavy product-speak on first two emails.
